title: Wickliffe's ear and the drummer who lost an audition
summary: Wickliffe had a good ear for harmony. A drummer who took a tune too fast cost the band an audition.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Whitliff had maybe a pre-Ellington appreciation of broad harmonies.

Yes, he probably did. He had a good ear, too, see, and that's, because some drummers don't have a very good ear. I mean, they have a sense of rhythm, but for harmony and, well, maybe I shouldn't say that because I believe it was a bad drummers. One bad drummer made us lose an audition. We auditioned for a job, and the drummer didn't have any conception at the time. And after we played a couple of numbers real good, the man we were auditioning for asked us to play another certain number. And we all called it and said, everybody got it? Yes. And we let out, and he played it. His conception of it was bad. He played it too fast, and they ruined the band. The guys couldn't play it. It was too fast. It was way too fast, and we sounded bad, and finally somebody got lost, and I was awfully ashamed. It wasn't the band's fault. It was the drummer's fault. So the man said, you better go back and rehearse a little more, boys. The first two numbers is all right, but you better go back and rehearse some more. And we felt awful bad about it. Coming back on L, I was very disgusted.
